memos.headline: Defensive rotation favors XOM and UNH; mega-cap tech remains in downtrends below key moving averages
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe as of 2025-03-21. The mega-cap tech names (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, AMZN, GOOGL) are all trading well below their 50-day and 200-day means with 12-week relative strength vs SPY ranging from -5.8% to -9.7%, confirming persistent underperformance. In contrast, XOM stands out as the strongest chart in the group—trading 5% above its 50-day mean, RSI 62.7, only -7.9% from its 52w high, and crushing SPY with +10.3% 4-week and +13.7% 12-week relative strength. UNH is the other standout with +16.8% 4-week relative strength and a clear momentum reversal off its lows, though the -17.3% drawdown from highs and sub-200d mean price keep my conviction moderate. I would avoid the weakest relative-strength names (AAPL, NVDA, GOOGL) until they reclaim their 50-day averages, which would represent roughly 5-10% upside from here.

views.note: Strongest relative strength in the universe (+13.7% vs SPY over 12w), above both moving averages, RSI 62.7 not yet overbought; would reassess on a close below 110.
Powerful 4-week relative strength of +16.8% vs SPY and +10.8% absolute return suggest momentum reversal, but still 5.2% below 200d mean and -17.3% from highs caps conviction; invalidated below 490.

Low volatility defensive name holding up relatively well with only -7.2% drawdown and positive 4w/12w relative strength vs SPY, but RSI 42 and slight negative drift don't invite aggressive positioning.

Down 21.2% from 52w high, 7.3% below 50d mean, 7.9% below 200d mean with -8.0% 12w relative strength vs SPY and elevated 4.89% ATR—trend is clearly down; need a close above 127 (approx 50d mean) to reconsider.
Worst 12-week relative strength in the group at -9.6% vs SPY, RSI 40, trading below both key moving averages; would need a sustained close above 232 (50d area) to turn constructive.
RSI 39, 10.2% below 50d mean, -20.5% drawdown from highs, and -9.7% 12w relative strength vs SPY make this one of the weakest charts; reclaim of 183 (50d area) needed.
Longer-term trend is constructive (above 200d mean by 5.6%, +6.3% 12w rel strength) but the 4-week pullback of -8.6% and RSI 44 suggest it's in a corrective phase; watching 230 as support.
RSI 37.5 is the lowest in the universe, 10.3% below 50d mean with -8.2% 12w relative strength; needs to reclaim ~218 (50d area) before I'd consider a long.

Slightly better 4w relative strength (+1.8% vs SPY) than other mega-cap tech peers, but still 7.6% below 200d mean and in a clear intermediate downtrend; watching 408 (50d area) as the line in the sand.
Recent 4w relative strength vs SPY is positive at +4.7% but the stock is 6.9% below its 200d mean and -19.5% from highs; mixed signals keep me sidelined until a close above 357 (50d area).

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Show Strongest Earnings Power; XOM and UNH Flash Margin Warnings
memos.body: I see the clearest durable earnings power in NVDA (+77.9% YoY revenue, 56.2% net margin) and GOOGL (+11.8% revenue, 27.5% margin with only $14.8B debt), both delivering accelerating profitability on manageable leverage. MSFT continues to compound at +12.3% revenue growth with a 34.6% net margin and moderate $45B debt load, making it a reliable compounder. On the other side, XOM posted -1.1% revenue decline with a thin 9.1% net margin, and UNH grew revenue only 6.8% while net income barely moved (+1.6%) on a heavy $76.9B debt stack—both signal cash-flow compression risk. CAT's -5.0% revenue decline is a concern, though margin discipline (17.2% net margin, +4.4% net income growth) partially offsets; I need to see the top line stabilize before getting constructive. AMZN's 88.3% net income surge is impressive but starts from a low 10.7% margin base, so sustainability of that margin expansion is the key swing factor.

views.note: 77.9% YoY revenue growth and 56.2% net margin on just $8.5B debt is extraordinary earnings power; a sustained margin compression below 45% would change my view.
11.8% revenue growth, 27.5% net margin, and only $14.8B total debt make this the best risk-adjusted earnings profile in mega-cap tech.
12.3% revenue growth and 34.6% net margin with disciplined leverage at $45B debt; would reassess if cloud segment growth decelerates below high single digits.
88.3% net income growth is eye-catching but 10.7% net margin remains thin for the valuation; need to see margin durability above 10% for multiple quarters.
29.2% net margin is strong but +4.0% revenue growth is the slowest among mega-cap tech peers, limiting upside unless Services mix accelerates.
50.5% net income growth and 32.7% margin are impressive but partly reflect favorable credit conditions; normalization of provisions would compress earnings.
21.2% net margin and 33.5% net income growth are solid for staples, but only 2.1% revenue growth limits earnings compounding potential.
Revenue declining 1.1% with a 9.1% net margin and $36.8B debt signals earnings vulnerability to further commodity weakness.
Only 1.6% net income growth on 6.8% revenue growth implies margin compression, and $76.9B debt load leaves little room for error.
Revenue fell 5.0% YoY and $31.7B debt is nearly 2x quarterly revenue; need top-line stabilization before turning constructive.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 4.50% With Sticky Inflation—Favor Defensives and Banks Over Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has been unchanged at 4.50% for three months, even as the trailing 12-month CPI print sits at 2.8% and the 3-month annualized pace (~4.0%) suggests inflation is re-accelerating. Unemployment at 4.2% is stable over three months but up 30 bps year-over-year, signaling a slow-motion softening rather than outright deterioration. The 10y yield at 4.25% has fallen 27 bps over three months while the 2s10s spread has steepened to +29 bps, consistent with the market pricing eventual easing but not imminently. In this higher-for-longer, mild-slowdown regime I prefer banks (benefiting from a positively sloped curve and stable short rates), staples (defensive in a decelerating economy), and would be cautious on high-multiple growth names whose valuations are most sensitive to the discount rate staying elevated. A CPI print falling below 2.5% YoY or unemployment jumping above 4.5% would shift my call toward an imminent easing regime, favoring duration-sensitive growth.

views.note: Positive and steepening yield curve (+29 bps 2s10s, up 61 bps YoY) supports net interest margins while the pause keeps short-rate income elevated.
Defensive staple benefits from a mild-slowdown backdrop with stable employment; less rate-sensitive than growth names at current yields.
High-multiple duration-sensitive growth is vulnerable while the Fed holds at 4.50% and sticky inflation delays any easing.
Premium valuation faces headwinds from elevated real rates, but strong cash generation provides a floor; net neutral until the rate path clarifies.
Mild slowdown signals temper the cyclical upside, but energy acts as an inflation hedge if CPI stays sticky; balanced risks.
Classic cyclical faces demand risk as unemployment drifts higher and rates remain restrictive, limiting capex appetite.
Quality growth with recurring revenue, but elevated discount rates cap multiple expansion; wait for clearer easing signal.
Consumer-facing cyclicality and high multiple make it sensitive to both the slowdown and the rate pause; no strong directional call.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Washout Across Mega-Cap Tech Creates Selective Opportunity
memos.body: I am struck by the uniformly negative post-earnings price reactions across the tech and industrial universe this cycle: NVDA -8.5%, GOOGL -7.3%, MSFT -6.2%, CAT -4.6%, AMZN -4.1%, XOM -2.5%, and AAPL -0.7%. These sharp sell-the-news moves suggest expectations were crowded long heading into prints, and the negative tone reset may now be largely priced several weeks later. GOOGL stands out with a fresh 8-K on March 18 (Reg FD / Other Events), which could signal a proactive narrative shift after the brutal -7.3% earnings reaction—I read that as management trying to recapture the story. JPM is the cleanest name from a sentiment perspective: three 8-Ks in quick succession with no earnings-driven price shock, suggesting steady institutional communication rather than damage control. I have lower conviction on NVDA given the magnitude of the post-earnings drop and the subsequent director change filing on March 7, which adds governance noise on top of already sour sentiment.

views.note: Worst post-earnings reaction at -7.3% likely over-discounted negativity; fresh March 18 Reg FD filing hints at proactive narrative management, suggesting tone inflection.
No negative earnings price shock and steady cadence of three 8-Ks in two weeks signals stable-to-improving institutional sentiment with no crowded positioning.
Minimal -0.7% earnings reaction suggests sentiment was already balanced; the Feb 25 shareholder vote filing is routine and provides no directional signal.
The -8.5% post-earnings drop was the largest in the universe and the March 7 director departure/appointment adds governance uncertainty before sentiment can stabilize.
The -6.2% earnings reaction was severe but occurred nearly two months ago; without fresh catalysts the negative tone is likely already absorbed.
The -4.6% post-earnings drop reflected industrial cycle concerns; with no subsequent filings, sentiment has likely mean-reverted but I lack a fresh signal to take a directional view.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Surges 154% in Three Months—Structural Headwinds for Export-Exposed and China-Linked Names
memos.body: I am flagging a dramatic escalation in the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index, which at 458.66 has risen 153.7% over three months and 24.7% in the last month alone, signaling that the current policy environment—likely driven by tariff escalation, export controls, and broader trade-policy volatility—is not a one-quarter event but a structural shift. The VIX at 19.80 is up 26.4% month-over-month, and HY spreads have widened 51 bps in a month, confirming that credit markets are beginning to price geopolitical risk. WTI crude at $68.55 is down nearly 6% over the past month, which I read as demand-side concern rather than supply relief, consistent with a global growth scare tied to trade friction. I have highest conviction on avoiding names with concentrated China/export-control exposure (NVDA, AAPL, CAT) and am more constructive on domestically oriented financials and defensive consumer staples. A reversal in my view would require a concrete de-escalation in tariff or export-control policy, not merely rhetoric.

views.note: Most exposed to tightening semiconductor export controls targeting China; the 154% surge in policy uncertainty is a direct headwind to its data-center revenue pipeline.
Heavy supply-chain concentration in China and rising tariff risk make AAPL vulnerable to further trade-policy escalation reflected in the uncertainty index.
CAT's Reg FD disclosure in January and its global infrastructure exposure leave it squarely in the crosshairs of tariff and trade-policy volatility.
WTI at $68.55 and falling 6% monthly suggests demand-side weakness; energy security tailwinds partially offset by global growth concerns, keeping me neutral.
Domestically oriented with a steepening yield curve (+7 bps 3m on 10y-2y spread) supporting NII; multiple 8-K filings suggest active capital management.
Defensive consumer staples with predominantly domestic demand should outperform in a high-policy-uncertainty regime where VIX is elevated and credit spreads are widening.
Less direct export-control exposure than hardware peers, but recent Reg FD disclosure and elevated uncertainty warrant caution; I lack conviction either way.

We hold ~55% cash to buffer against further volatility, concentrating risk in the four names where multiple analysts converge.
